Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

record verb

write down, put on record

also write down, note down, put on record

classical

Cic. Sull. 42: in tabulās pūblicās relātum (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 7.3.7: in commentārium (Lewis & Short)

referō, referre, rettulī, relātum

verb, irregular, transitive; with <span lang="la">in</span> + accusative

enter, record (in a register or notebook)

With in tabulās, in commentārium, in librum: to enter something in a record. Its commoner senses are “bring back”, “report” and “refer” (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • litterīs mandō, mandāre, mandāvī, mandātum — commit to writing

    also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.52: litterīs (Lewis & Short, s.v. mandō)

    To write something down so that it is kept: of history, a speech, what someone said.

  • perscrībō, perscrībere, perscrīpsī, perscrīptum — write out in full; put on record

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. perscrībō; Traupman 177: est perscrīpta (a motion put on record)

Examples

  • cum scīrem ita indicium in tabulās pūblicās relātum

    since I knew that the evidence had been entered in the public records in that formCic. Sull. 42 (Lewis & Short)

See also write, record, enter, record.

SourcesLewis & Short: refero · Lewis & Short: mando · Lewis & Short: perscribo
